proposals.label: Youth skills and aspirations in AI
proposals.definition: AI discussed in relation to young people: investing in youth AI skills, youth enthusiasm for generative AI, and ensuring youth are not left behind.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where young people, students, or youth skills are the explicit subject of the AI mention.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude youth passages that do not mention AI or related technologies.
proposals.boundary_cases: If youth exclusion is framed as a global digital divide, also code AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: We are investing in their skills in information technology, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, and green innovation.
Our young people are excited about the prospect of fast-unfolding generative AI.

proposals.label: Unequal access and an AI divide
proposals.definition: Concern that AI benefits are not equally accessible and that developing countries and their youth will be excluded, creating an AI divide.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI benefits must be shared fairly or warnings of a digital/AI divide between countries or generations.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for technology transfer mechanisms without an inequality framing (code AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
proposals.boundary_cases: A passage warning of an excluded generation is coded here even if framed around youth.

examples.quote: We do not want today's digital divide to become tomorrow's artificial intelligence divide.
one of our deepest concerns is the widening digital divide facing youth in developing world

proposals.label: Technology transfer and affordable access
proposals.definition: Calls for technology transfer, skills development and affordable access to AI and modern technologies for developing countries.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit requests for technology transfer, skills, or affordable access tied to AI or advanced technology.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic LDC graduation support lists not connected to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for international cooperation creating 'space for developing countries' in AI applications can be coded here.

examples.quote: it is essential to ensure technology transfer, skills development, and affordable access to modern technologies for developing countries

proposals.label: Protecting human labour from AI
proposals.definition: Concern that AI development could diminish demand for human labour, alongside hopes AI can create jobs and livelihoods.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements on AI's effects on jobs, labour demand, or livelihoods.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude migration and labour passages without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of youth as 'job creators' through AI skills lean to AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION unless labour impact is discussed.

examples.quote: the world needs to ensure that the development of artificial intelligence does not diminish the scope of or demand for human labour

proposals.label: Autonomous intelligence as existential threat
proposals.definition: Warnings that self-propagating autonomous AI developed irresponsibly could threaten human existence.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to AI operating without human intervention posing existential or catastrophic risk.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude military autonomous weapons discussions (code AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
proposals.boundary_cases: General calls for 'caution' about AI impacts without an existential claim are borderline and should be coded only if loss of human control is mentioned.

examples.quote: unless autonomous intelligence develops in a responsible manner, it could pose existential threats to human existence

proposals.label: AI deepfakes and disinformation
proposals.definition: AI-driven deepfakes and fake news amplifying disinformation and hate speech that erode social trust.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI to deepfakes, fake news, or false narratives.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude disinformation passages with no AI reference.
proposals.boundary_cases: A continuation passage about 'distortions' that does not itself mention AI should not be coded.

examples.quote: compounded by the deliberate use of fake news and artificial intelligence-driven deepfakes, which make the situation even more dangerous

proposals.label: UN policy framework for AI benefits
proposals.definition: Calls for the United Nations to adopt a policy framework so AI benefits are harnessed across countries.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit calls on the UN to create AI policy or frameworks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic partnership with the UN on youth platforms not about AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for fair, unbiased AI without naming the UN go to AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS or AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: It is now time for the United Nations to adopt an effective policy framework so that the benefits of the development and rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and social media can be harnessed positively

proposals.label: Unbiased and fair AI
proposals.definition: Demands that AI and related technologies not be biased.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit statements that AI systems must not be biased or must be fair.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude fairness framed purely as access between countries (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
proposals.boundary_cases: A single sentence combining bias and fair sharing can be coded both here and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: these must not be biased, and their benefits must be shared fairly with all

proposals.label: AI-driven national economic transformation
proposals.definition: Speaker describes the country's own plans to digitize and make its economy AI-driven, and current national deployment of AI systems in services and environmental monitoring.
proposals.inclusion: Include descriptions of national AI deployment, AI-driven economic visions, or domestic AI investments.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for global AI rules without domestic content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Domestic AI use in health, education and environment may also be coded AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.

examples.quote: transforming its economy into one that is fully digitized and driven by artificial intelligence (AI)
We are using and expanding artificial intelligence systems to deliver essential services such as healthcare, education and social welfare.

proposals.label: Digital literacy for an AI generation
proposals.definition: Investing in digital literacy from a young age so a generation can use AI to deliver services and compete in the digital economy.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on building AI-related skills or literacy among young people.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general education reforms without AI linkage.
proposals.boundary_cases: Domestic regulatory and start-up measures in the same passage belong to AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: invest in people’s digital literacy from a young age to build a generation that can use artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI overcoming distance and scale for small states
proposals.definition: AI is framed as especially valuable for small and island states by closing distance and overcoming scale in service delivery.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI benefits to small-state or island geographic constraints.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general AI development benefits not tied to smallness or dispersion.
proposals.boundary_cases: Generic health/education benefits without the small-state framing go to AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.

examples.quote: For small states, AI can close distance. It can help overcome scale.

proposals.label: Every country's voice in AI rules
proposals.definition: Call that all countries have a voice in shaping global AI rules and that the digital future not create dependence.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for inclusive participation in global AI rule-making.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude domestic regulatory framework statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Warnings about dependence also fit AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: Every country must have a voice in shaping the global rules for AI.

proposals.label: Avoiding new forms of technological dependence
proposals.definition: Concern that the AI/digital transformation should not create new dependence for small states.
proposals.inclusion: Include warnings about dependence on external technology or partners in the AI context.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic access-gap statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Paired with calls for a voice in rules, also code AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: The digital future should strengthen our ability to serve our people better, not create new forms of dependence.

proposals.label: Groundwork for AI regulation and agency
proposals.definition: Calls to lay the groundwork for AI regulation and multilateral governance, including a future international AI agency.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for AI regulation, multilateral AI governance, or new international AI institutions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general statements about harnessing progress with ethics that do not call for rules or institutions.
proposals.boundary_cases: Offers to host an international AI agency count here and, where linked to UN officials, AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: We need to lay the groundwork for the regulation of artificial intelligence
We would like to host the headquarters of a future international artificial intelligence agency.

proposals.label: Supporting the SG's Envoy on Technology
proposals.definition: Support for UN Secretariat AI/technology functions such as the Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology.
proposals.inclusion: Include pledges of resources or support to UN technology offices or envoys on AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude non-UN governance calls.
proposals.boundary_cases: Support framed as 'developing multilateral governance' is coded both here and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Spain is committed to supporting the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology with resources and know-how

proposals.label: Human-centric, ethical AI progress
proposals.definition: AI and digital transformation should be human-centric, rights-oriented and combined with ethics.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for human-centric, rights-oriented, or ethically guided AI progress.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude governance calls without ethical/rights content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Historical analogies about fear of new technology followed by an ethics call count here and AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: a more human-centric and rights-oriented digital transformation
to combine progress with an ethic that is essential in that great leap

proposals.label: Disruption breeds fear; harness progress
proposals.definition: Framing AI as a disruptive advance that, like writing or electricity, generates fear but can be harnessed; possibilities weighed against hidden risks.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages weighing AI's possibilities against risks or placing fears of AI in historical perspective.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely risk-focused or purely benefit-focused statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that possibilities 'do not outweigh hidden risks' lean risk-ward but still count as explicit weighing.

examples.quote: the emergence of a disruptive advance generates fear and mistrust. This is not the first time.

proposals.label: AI accelerating the 2030 Agenda
proposals.definition: AI as a transformative revolution that can accelerate the 2030 Agenda if directed toward fair and equitable digital transformation.
proposals.inclusion: Include claims that AI can advance the SDGs/2030 Agenda.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude listing of AI among challenges without development link.
proposals.boundary_cases: Conditional framing ('if we know how to direct it') still counts here.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence which can accelerate progress on the 2030 agenda if we know how to direct it towards a fair and equitable digital transformation

proposals.label: AI as revolution for health and development
proposals.definition: AI described as a genuine technological revolution that, properly used, brings unprecedented development in healthcare, environment and production, and must benefit citizens.
proposals.inclusion: Passages framing AI as transformative and beneficial for health, environment, productivity or citizens' lives.
proposals.exclusion: Passages only listing AI among issues (use AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Conditional benefit statements ('if employed properly') count here and may also take AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: it will bring about unprecedented development in healthcare, the environment, productive processes, and in the lives of human beings in general

proposals.label: Avoid widening digital inequality
proposals.definition: Warning that AI must not widen the digital divide and global digital inequality.
proposals.inclusion: Passages urging that AI not widen digital divides or inequality between countries.
proposals.exclusion: Concrete capacity-building requests (use AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
proposals.boundary_cases: Fair regulation so AI does not serve a few may take AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION instead.

examples.quote: we must not widen the digital divide and digital inequality throughout the world

proposals.label: AI regulation as UN strategic priority
proposals.definition: Calls for the UN to make regulation of AI and new information technologies a strategic priority.
proposals.inclusion: Passages asking the UN to prioritize AI/ICT regulation.
proposals.exclusion: International regulation calls not tied to the UN (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Bundling AI with cybercrime and social media regulation still counts when the UN is named.

examples.quote: the regulation of new information technologies, social media and artificial intelligence must become a strategic priority for the United Nations

proposals.label: Against control by few and destabilization
proposals.definition: Fair regulation must prevent new technologies including AI from serving the interests and control of a few or being used to destabilize legitimate governments.
proposals.inclusion: Passages opposing AI serving the control of a few or its use to destabilize governments and social harmony.
proposals.exclusion: Disinformation concerns framed without state sovereignty (use AI_DISINFORMATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Use for regime destabilization framing can also take AI_DISINFORMATION if information manipulation is explicit.

examples.quote: we must promote fair and equitable regulation that does not allow the focus of those new tools to be for the interests and control of a few
Neither can we accept the use of those new technologies to destabilize legitimate Governments

proposals.label: AI listed among humanity's major issues
proposals.definition: AI named in a list of major global issues without elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Passages listing AI alongside peace, development, climate or energy.
proposals.exclusion: Passages elaborating on AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: An introductory list previewing a later AI section is still a list mention for that passage.

examples.quote: free trade, energy security and, more recently, artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Anti-colonial claim to AI's benefits
proposals.definition: AI framed as a product of human intelligence built on colonized peoples' resources, with demands that those peoples share in its benefits and warnings that AI in the hands of 'malevolent actors' becomes a weapon against peoples.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages invoking colonial extraction, imperial actors or domination in relation to AI and demanding participation or restitution of benefits.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude neutral access requests without a domination or anti-imperial framing (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Rhetoric describing AI as 'weapons of mass destruction' in the hands of hegemonic actors belongs here rather than AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS unless actual weapons systems are discussed.

examples.quote: Nicaragua demands the full participation of the peoples who have made those advances of the conquistadors possible with our blood and resources.
in the hands of the same malevolent actors as always, constitute weapons of mass destruction against countries, peoples and communities

proposals.label: Right to enjoy AI development
proposals.definition: Demand for inclusion and the right of peoples to enjoy the benefits of AI and technological development to improve work, study and life.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages asserting a right to share AI benefits for living and working conditions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages only criticizing power concentration without a benefit-sharing claim.
proposals.boundary_cases: Skepticism about the term 'artificial intelligence' itself does not change coding if benefit-sharing is demanded.

examples.quote: We demand what is ours — the right to fully enjoy this development, improving the conditions of work, study and life of our peoples

proposals.label: Transnational tech domination and algorithmic control
proposals.definition: Critique that a few (mostly US) transnational companies control platforms, content and algorithms, producing cultural domination and manipulation of behaviour.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on dictatorship of the algorithm, few transnationals imposing systems and controlling content.
proposals.exclusion: Inclusive governance calls without a domination critique (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Anti-capitalist critiques of AI misuse can take this code if concentration of power is explicit.

examples.quote: A few transnationals, almost all of them from the US, impose their operating systems and control the content that is seen, read and heard
We are suffering from the dictatorship of the algorithm.

proposals.label: Inclusive UN-based AI governance for all
proposals.definition: Calls for common norms and more inclusive global governance of AI, including voice for developing regions like Africa in AI governance decisions.
proposals.inclusion: Passages calling for UN common norms on AI, inclusive governance of disruptive technologies, or African voice in global AI governance.
proposals.exclusion: Critiques of corporate concentration without a governance call.
proposals.boundary_cases: Demands that Africa be heard in global AI governance take this and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE if inequality is also raised.

examples.quote: establish at the UN as soon as possible common norms in order to unlock the transformative potential of new technologies, especially artificial intelligence
promote governance that is more inclusive in the use of the new ICTs and telecommunications, particularly the disruptive technologies such as artificial intelligence
climate issues and global governance of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI misuse under capitalism threatening humanity
proposals.definition: AI misuse, driven by capitalism, portrayed as a systemic threat that could worsen climate change and render most people unnecessary.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI misuse to capitalism, planetary destruction or mass human redundancy.
proposals.exclusion: Technical loss-of-control safety concerns (use AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL) or narrow job loss (use AI_ECONOMY_LABOR).
proposals.boundary_cases: If the passage focuses on job displacement without systemic critique, use AI_ECONOMY_LABOR instead.

examples.quote: the unstoppable force of capitalism with the misuse of artificial intelligence would increase the climate change, would liquidate the planet

proposals.label: Rejecting AI research for warfare
proposals.definition: Rejection of AI research or development for warfare purposes, framed within opposition to the arms race and militarization.
proposals.inclusion: Passages opposing military AI, AI for warfare, or AI as part of an arms race.
proposals.exclusion: Non-military AI risks or general disarmament passages without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Arms-race resource arguments count only when AI for warfare is explicitly named.

examples.quote: rejecting the militarization of outer space and research in the area of artificial intelligence for warfare purposes

proposals.label: Binding rules on autonomous weapons
proposals.definition: Speaker calls for prohibitions and regulation of autonomous weapons systems and military AI, stressing meaningful human control over life-or-death decisions.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to autonomous weapons, military automation, militarization of new technologies, or human control over lethal force.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude civilian AI governance calls without any military dimension.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for governance frameworks covering both military and civilian AI should be coded here and in AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: No algorithm should ever make life or death decisions.
The militarization of new technologies poses specific problems.
governance frameworks for artificial intelligence in both the military and civilian spheres

proposals.label: AI governance as a defining global challenge
proposals.definition: AI governance is presented as one of the major global challenges requiring new international frameworks.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming AI governance as a key global challenge or calling for new governance frameworks for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about domestic AI use only.
proposals.boundary_cases: Governance calls tied to cybersecurity and cybercrime may also be coded AI_CYBER_SECURITY.

examples.quote: nuclear weapons, the triple planetary crisis, and the governance of artificial intelligence
we urgently need new governance frameworks on cybersecurity, cybercrime and artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Leading UN AI panel and dialogue
proposals.definition: Speaker highlights UN mechanisms for AI such as the Global Digital Compact, the Independent International Scientific Panel and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, including its own role in establishing them.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit references to UN AI processes, bodies or resolutions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic multilateralism without a specific UN AI mechanism.
proposals.boundary_cases: Draft General Assembly resolutions on autonomous weapons are primarily AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS but may be coded here too.

examples.quote: has led the process that established the independent international scientific panel and the global dialogue on AI governance
The recently adopted Global Digital Compact (resolution 79/1, annex I) sets the multilateral system in motion to address artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI enabling cyberattacks, terrorism and disinformation
proposals.definition: AI is framed as a threat to peace and security via cyberattacks on infrastructure, cyber terrorism, crime and mass disinformation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI to cyberattacks, cyber terrorism, crime or attacks on democratic institutions.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude military weapons uses, which belong to AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of AI-driven mass disinformation should also be coded AI_DISINFORMATION.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence can boost cyber terrorism and other crimes that we cannot yet envisage.
It can become a vector of mass disinformation and enable cyber attacks that paralyze critical infrastructure.

proposals.label: AI benefits versus access divide
proposals.definition: AI is framed as able to strengthen economies and knowledge access while also dividing those with and without access.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that explicitly contrast AI's development benefits with its risks, including a digital divide.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude one-sided risk or benefit statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the risk emphasized is access inequality, also code AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: But it can also divide us between those who have access and those who do not.

proposals.label: Co-facilitating the UN Global Dialogue
proposals.definition: The speaker country's role in leading or co-facilitating the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance and the message it promoted there.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to leading, co-chairing or participating in UN AI governance processes.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general UN reform demands without AI content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements on what AI 'must' do made within the Dialogue context may also be coded with the substantive theme (e.g. AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS).

examples.quote: Heading up alongside Estonia, the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance

proposals.label: AI expanding capacities and competitiveness
proposals.definition: AI framed as a tool to expand capacities, create opportunities and build competitive economies.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI should expand capacities, create opportunities or competitiveness.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude workforce training plans (AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Competitiveness framed nationally may overlap with AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: this technology must expand capacities and create opportunities to build environments that can be competitive in the future

proposals.label: Training youth for superintelligence economy
proposals.definition: National ambition to join the technological transformation by training young people in superintelligence, robotics and data science.
proposals.inclusion: Include plans or aims to train youth or workforce for AI and related technologies.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general education reform without technology link.
proposals.boundary_cases: Investment-attraction pitches naming technology are coded here only if skills/training is explicit.

examples.quote: We want to train young people for super intelligence, for robotics, for data science
Colombia does not want to watch the technological transformation of our time from the sidelines.

proposals.label: Promoting UN assessment of AI's SDG impact
proposals.definition: Diplomatic initiative within the UN to institutionalize assessment of AI and rapid technological change on the 2030 Agenda.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to sponsoring or promoting UN resolutions, reviews or assessments concerning AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national SDG institutional arrangements without an AI element.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where the initiative is framed mainly around SDG outcomes, also code AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS.

examples.quote: promoted the annual assessment of the impact of rapid technological change, especially artificial intelligence, on the achievement of the 2030 Agenda

proposals.label: AI's impact on the 2030 Agenda
proposals.definition: Linking AI to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages connecting AI to the 2030 Agenda or SDG achievement.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic sustainable-development commitments that do not mention AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: The preceding sentence about national 2030 Agenda architecture has no AI content and is not coded on its own.

examples.quote: especially artificial intelligence, on the achievement of the 2030 Agenda

proposals.label: Unprecedented opportunities and significant risks
proposals.definition: AI is explicitly framed as offering transformative opportunities while posing risks to security, equity, human rights and institutions.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that explicitly pair AI benefits (progress, education, productivity) with AI risks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that mention only benefits or only risks of AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: If risks named include inequality, also code AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: offer up unprecedented opportunities for human progress. However, they also offer up significant risks for security, equity and human rights
It can transform education, multiply productivity and close historic gaps, but also entrench inequalities and serve those that seek to weaken our institutions.

proposals.label: Multilateral, ethical, values-based AI governance
proposals.definition: Calls for multilateral and ethical international governance of AI guided by the common good and shared values.
proposals.inclusion: Include calls for international or multilateral governance frameworks for AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national AI regulation without an international dimension.
proposals.boundary_cases: Governance calls that emphasise inclusive access are coded here and AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: it's essential to move towards multilateral and ethical governance of these tools
We need international governance that enables us to innovate without renouncing our values

proposals.label: Inclusive access, avoiding new digital gaps
proposals.definition: Concern that AI must be accessible inclusively and must not create new digital gaps or leave those with fewer resources behind.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements about guaranteeing access to AI and avoiding new gaps or leaving the poor behind.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic development financing requests without AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Close historic gaps' as an AI benefit alone is AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS rather than this code.

examples.quote: would guarantee their inclusive access to them, that would avoid new digital gaps
does not leave those that have the least resources behind. They also need to be able to access this technology

proposals.label: Rights-based ethical framework for AI
proposals.definition: Calls for ethical, transparent, responsible AI regulation grounded in human rights, dignity, privacy and data protection.
proposals.inclusion: Passages demanding an ethical framework or regulation for AI respecting human rights, personal data, dignity and freedom.
proposals.exclusion: Passages mainly about disinformation (use AI_DISINFORMATION) or bias/cultural erasure (use AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_EXCLUSION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for multilateral ethical frameworks take this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: guiding the progress of artificial intelligence in an ethical, transparent and responsible manner, respecting human rights, protecting personal data
We need a framework that takes the human rights perspective into account in technological research and development,
with a view to protecting and promoting the dignity and the rights of peoples and individuals

proposals.label: Algorithmic bias and digital erasure of cultures
proposals.definition: AI reproduces prejudices and stereotypes from biased training data and risks the digital extermination of non-hegemonic cultures, requiring traceability, audits and human correction.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on AI bias, stereotypes, algorithm traceability, data audits or loss of cultural diversity.
proposals.exclusion: General rights language without bias or cultural exclusion (use AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
proposals.boundary_cases: Exclusion of the weakest from the AI world may also take AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: today artificial intelligence reproduces prejudices and stereotypes resulting from the reinforcement of existing biases in the databases with which they are trained
the digital extermination of non-hegemonic cultures and, along with it, the loss of humankind’s valuable diversity

proposals.label: Distrust of corporate self-regulation
proposals.definition: Scepticism that large technology companies can be trusted to regulate AI themselves.
proposals.inclusion: Passages questioning or rejecting industry self-regulation of AI.
proposals.exclusion: Concentration of AI power among states (use AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: If the passage stresses dominance of few companies rather than regulation, use AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: Are we going to trust the large companies to regulate themselves in this area? History teaches us that that does not work.

proposals.label: AI disinformation and election manipulation
proposals.definition: AI facilitates disinformation campaigns manipulating public opinion, especially during elections, destabilizing democracies.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on AI-driven disinformation, information integrity, or election manipulation.
proposals.exclusion: Privacy harms like deepfake nudes (use AI_CHILD_PROTECTION or AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
proposals.boundary_cases: A brief mention that technology should address disinformation counts here.

examples.quote: also facilitates the spread of disinformation campaigns aimed at manipulating public opinion, especially in election periods

proposals.label: AI abuse harming minors' privacy
proposals.definition: Concrete harms where AI is used to violate the privacy and integrity of children, e.g., AI-generated nude images of schoolgirls.
proposals.inclusion: Passages describing AI misuse against children or classmates, such as image manipulation.
proposals.exclusion: Generic privacy or data protection statements (use AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
proposals.boundary_cases: Anecdotes used to motivate an ethical framework take both codes.

examples.quote: used artificial intelligence to remove the clothing of their female classmates

proposals.label: Technology as opportunity or new injustice
proposals.definition: AI and technological change framed as comparable to the industrial revolution, able to create fairer societies or new injustices and inequalities.
proposals.inclusion: Passages framing AI as both a major opportunity and potential source of harm or inequality.
proposals.exclusion: One-sided statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Invoking Asimov's law to pair AI's contribution with harm prevention counts here.

examples.quote: if we get it wrong, they can also be the source of new injustices
Artificial intelligence and new technologies can be a significant contribution to the world.

proposals.label: Chile as regional AI benchmark
proposals.definition: Speaker highlights national initiatives and leadership in AI.
proposals.inclusion: Passages citing national AI initiatives or claiming regional leadership.
proposals.exclusion: International proposals.
proposals.boundary_cases: National regulatory commitments may also take AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: my country today serves as a Latin American benchmark for the future of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: New regulatory schemes: sandboxes, co-regulation
proposals.definition: Argument that exponential technological change requires new, agile regulatory techniques (sandboxes, co-regulation) to protect people and ensure responsible, equitable use; not specifically international.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages proposing specific regulatory methods or new regulatory schemes to keep pace with AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for international treaties or global bodies (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: If the regulatory innovation is proposed for global adoption, code both this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: require us to create new regulatory schemes to protect people
Those new techniques, such as sandboxes and co-regulation, must have as their ultimate goal the responsible use of emerging technologies

proposals.label: Ethical application of AI
proposals.definition: Highlighting the ethical application of AI as a standout challenge.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages foregrounding ethical use of AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude regulatory-technique discussion without ethical framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Equitable application' can overlap with AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE if between-country access is meant.

examples.quote: the question of the ethical application of artificial intelligence and of advances in technology in general stands out here

proposals.label: Most powerful technology, ungoverned
proposals.definition: Alarm that AI, the most powerful technology ever, has no one governing it, and that it is an ethical and geopolitical rather than merely technical issue.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI lacks governance or must be governed collectively as a political/ethical matter.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national regulatory choices described as domestic policy (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
proposals.boundary_cases: Framing AI as 'an ethical challenge' can also be coded AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: we're seeing the emergence of the most powerful technology that humankind has ever known, and no one is governing it
It is an ethical challenge and a geopolitical issue.

proposals.label: Rejecting innovation-versus-responsibility dilemma
proposals.definition: Positioning AI policy between fear and recklessness: neither rushing nor turning away from AI's opportunities, a 'responsible pace'.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that reject a trade-off between innovation and responsibility or describe balancing speed against capacity to manage.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely promotional or purely alarmist statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Domestic regulatory balance described as 'responsible pace' also counts under AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: We reject the false dilemma between innovation and responsibility.
We want to lead from a position of knowledge and not fear.

proposals.label: National AI growth and responsible pace
proposals.definition: The speaker's own country's AI approach: expected growth gains, enabling regulation, investment in talent and energy.
proposals.inclusion: Include descriptions of domestic AI regulation, investment and expected national growth.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic global claims about AI's economic potential.
proposals.boundary_cases: National food production projections enabled by AI may be coded AI_DEVELOPMENT_SDGS instead.

examples.quote: We have regulations that make things possible that do not hamper progress. We have investment in talent and in energy

proposals.label: UN as forum on AI's fate
proposals.definition: The UN presented as the place to bring humankind together to discuss AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include claims that the UN must convene or lead discussion on AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude UN reform statements not linked to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Contrasting slow UN reform with fast AI emergence counts only if the UN is assigned an AI role.

examples.quote: The United Nations must be able to bring humankind together to discuss a technology that will decide the fate of this century.

proposals.label: AI as defining force of the era
proposals.definition: AI framed as the defining transformation of the age, comparable to steam or the transistor, and embedded in decision-making across warfare, economy and daily life.
proposals.inclusion: Include historical-epochal framings of AI as the driving force or great transformation of our time.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude brief listings of AI among technologies without epochal framing (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Epochal framing followed by specific benefits should also be coded with the benefit theme.

examples.quote: Steam powered the industrial revolution. The transistor powered the digital age. No force in our time is as profound as artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: AI multiplying food production
proposals.definition: AI's potential to accelerate development, e.g. vastly expanding food production.
proposals.inclusion: Include concrete claims of AI enabling development outcomes like food security or faster progress.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic growth percentages for the national economy (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
proposals.boundary_cases: Inclusion demands ('no one should be left out') accompanying benefits may also be AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: Paraguay today feeds 100 million people, and with this tool, it could feed 1 billion.

proposals.label: Robotization forcing rethink of work
proposals.definition: AI and robotization transforming production and threatening work, requiring rethinking of education, production processes and job preservation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages linking AI/automation to changes in work, production or employment.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude generic technological-revolution statements without labour/production content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of rethinking education alongside work can also be coded AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.

examples.quote: Robotization and the accelerated process of installation of artificial intelligence force us to rethink education, production processes and the preservation of work.

proposals.label: AI misuse listed among global crises
proposals.definition: AI's inappropriate application named briefly within a catalogue of global problems without elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages listing AI among crises such as conflict, inequality, climate change or cyberwarfare with no further discussion.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that elaborate AI's specific risks or benefits.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the list item is accompanied by a specific policy proposal on AI, code the relevant substantive theme.

examples.quote: risks of cyberwarfare and the inappropriate application of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: Embedded AI values threatening democratic will
proposals.definition: Concern that values trained into AI systems silently shape decisions, severing democratic accountability; the choice of values must be freedom and democracy with trainers held accountable.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages arguing AI embeds its trainers' values, can covertly displace democratic decision-making, or that those training AI must be accountable.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude election disinformation and deepfakes (AI_DISINFORMATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that AI must serve human dignity without the democracy argument go to AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: Like a child, artificial intelligence repeats what it has learned from those who trained it.
the will of the people risks being replaced without ever having been defeated

proposals.label: AI serving human dignity
proposals.definition: Ethical principle that AI must serve rather than replace human dignity.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI must serve human dignity or human values, including religious ethical references.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude governance calls lacking an ethical principle.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where dignity is invoked in a democracy-accountability argument, code both.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence must serve human dignity and not replace it.

proposals.label: Critique of UN stance on AI
proposals.definition: AI's advent announced as an agenda item in a speech critical of the UN, signalling scepticism of the organisation's role on AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages that question or criticise the UN's position or competence regarding AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude supportive statements about UN AI bodies (AI_UN_ROLE).
proposals.boundary_cases: A mere agenda preview naming AI within a UN critique is coded here with low confidence.

examples.quote: third, its position in the face of the advent of artificial intelligence

proposals.label: AI as integration and development tool
proposals.definition: Optimistic framing of AI, alongside globalization and IT, as a tool for integration and development of peoples, conditional on good use.
proposals.inclusion: Passages describing AI as a tool helping integration or development, including with a 'if used well' caveat.
proposals.exclusion: Passages where risk is the dominant framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: A brief caveat about good use does not make the passage a duality passage unless harms are named.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence and real-time communication are tools that help the integration and development of our peoples — of course, if they are used well

examples.text: promoted the annual assessment of the impact of rapid technological change, especially artificial intelligence, on the achievement of the 2030 Agenda.

The current arms race is deplorable and consumes tremendous amounts of resources. Imagine what we could have achieved in terms of making the world more humane if those resources had been channelled into combating disease and hunger and improving food safety and security. Who would not aspire to those sustainable goals? Like many other countries, Suriname calls for an end to the arms race, while also rejecting the militarization of outer space and research in the area of artificial intelligence for warfare purposes.

As all those calamities are unfolding, we are witnessing an astonishing technological revolution. Robotization and the accelerated process of installation of artificial intelligence force us to rethink education, production processes and the preservation of work. How to address changes and harmonize interests in this new scenario in which we find ourselves is the real challenge we face.

I turn finally to the third challenge, which is related to technological change and can only be compared to the industrial revolution of the mid-eighteenth century. It will drastically change how we relate to one another and our ways of thinking, producing and working. Only a few days ago, a mother in a small town in Spain reported a group of young boys who used artificial intelligence to remove the clothing of their female classmates, harming their honour as well as their right to themselves, their integrity and their privacy. All technological developments throughout the history of humankind have been a major opportunity to create fairer societies; however, if we get it wrong, they can also be the source of new injustices. In that context, we are all obliged to create multilateral consensus and an ethical framework for the development and use of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence. We need a framework that takes the human rights perspective into account in technological research and development,
with a view to protecting and promoting the dignity and the rights of peoples and individuals, as well as sustainable development needs.

There is no doubt that societies must make progress, but we must do it in a responsible way. That is why we must understand and better manage the opportunities offered by technologies for our benefit, before they become a threat and further entrench existing inequalities. That is, for example, what we have been doing in Chile since we established the Congress on the Future, and I am certain that everyone here has similar initiatives in their own countries. Humbly, but also proudly, I can say that my country today serves as a Latin American benchmark for the future of artificial intelligence, and we will work tirelessly in that direction. Democracy is memory and future. That underlies our view that technological development must be a tool for unity, not division, and one that promotes the empowerment of all of society, addresses the phenomenon of disinformation, supports the most vulnerable sectors and does not further entrench inequalities at the national and global levels.

In addition, we urgently need new governance frameworks on cybersecurity, cybercrime and artificial intelligence. The militarization of new technologies poses specific problems. Therefore, in accordance with what was agreed in the Belém communiqué and, together with Austria and Mexico, we will submit a draft resolution to the General Assembly that addresses the issue of autonomous weapons systems.

Furthermore, Europe has the responsibility to push globally for a more human-centric and rights-oriented digital transformation. We need to lay the groundwork for the regulation of artificial intelligence, the vast challenges and possibilities of which do not outweigh its hidden risks. In that regard, Spain is committed to supporting the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology with resources and know-how in developing multilateral governance in that area. We would like to host the headquarters of a future international artificial intelligence agency.

“In the face of all the advances in science, techniques and technologies, including those portentously called “artificial intelligence” — as if they were not the result of human intelligence — Nicaragua demands the full participation of the peoples who have made those advances of the conquistadors possible with our blood and resources. We demand what is ours — the right to fully enjoy this development, improving the conditions of work, study and life of our peoples, with all their rights. In addition to inclusion, Nicaragua also proposes the rational and beneficial use of those resources of humankind, which in the hands of the same malevolent actors as always, constitute weapons of mass destruction against countries, peoples and communities.

We come once again to the Assembly with a positive and optimistic vision of humankind, but we must not be naive. Objectively, we live in a better world, although of course our current reality has its challenges and threats. We are convinced that globalization, information technology, artificial intelligence and real-time communication are tools that help the integration and development of our peoples — of course, if they are used well. In that respect, there is a growing sense of responsibility among world leaders. I heard the Secretary-General emphasize that issue earlier today. We are in a world where speeches are actions; where, standing here, a world leader can generate consequences — be it an international conflict, a bank run or something else — just with his words.

The protection of cyberspace, the fight against cybercrime, the regulation of new information technologies, social media and artificial intelligence must become a strategic priority for the United Nations. If we truly advocate for the defence of human rights and democratic principles, we must promote fair and equitable regulation that does not allow the focus of those new tools to be for the interests and control of a few. Neither can we accept the use of those new technologies to destabilize legitimate Governments and destroy social harmony and peace.

We are particularly enthused by emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications. Our young people are excited about the prospect of fast-unfolding generative AI. They aspire to walk and work as global citizens. The world needs to ensure that no young people in countries like Bangladesh are left behind in reaping meaningful benefits from the AI-led transformation. At the same time, the world needs to ensure that the development of artificial intelligence does not diminish the scope of or demand for human labour.

As the scientific community and the world of technology keep moving in developing autonomous intelligence — artificial intelligence that propagates on its own without any human intervention — we all need to be cautious of the possible impact on every human person or our societies, today and beyond. We believe that unless autonomous intelligence develops in a responsible manner, it could pose existential threats to human existence. We need newer forms of collaboration where global business and knowledge-holders connect to people’s needs. International cooperation should create space for the developing countries in ways that can bring transformative applications or solutions for jobs, endemic socioeconomic challenges or livelihoods.

Chile is also committed to the development of regulations for guiding the progress of artificial intelligence in an ethical, transparent and responsible manner, respecting human rights, protecting personal data and promoting the integrity of information and its use in the digital era. No doubt many of us have artificial intelligence applications on our mobile phones, but today artificial intelligence reproduces prejudices and stereotypes resulting from the reinforcement of existing biases in the databases with which they are trained. Are we going to trust the large companies to regulate themselves in this area? History teaches us that that does not work.

The international community must look out for the weakest among us, who are being excluded from this new world in formation, despite the fact that they too are entitled to take part in it. If we do not take action now, for example by demanding algorithm traceability, data audits and corrective human interventions, we might see a new kind of extermination in a few years — the digital extermination of non-hegemonic cultures and, along with it, the loss of humankind’s valuable diversity. Let us not allow that to happen.

Artificial intelligence and new technologies can be a significant contribution to the world. Let us recall Asimov’s first law of robotics, which, already in the middle of the previous century, urged us to establish that “[a] robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm”.

However, we must go farther. Costa Rica calls for a consensus to be reached on governance frameworks for artificial intelligence in both the military and civilian spheres. Those frameworks must regulate autonomous systems with transformative capabilities that operate without human intervention. The recently adopted Global Digital Compact (resolution 79/1, annex I) sets the multilateral system in motion to address artificial intelligence and is key for its research and development, not just its applications.

I shall conclude by making two observations. The first is that humankind faces old challenges such as those I have briefly mentioned. But new ones, such as the expansion of artificial intelligence are also emerging. As so often in the past, the emergence of a disruptive advance generates fear and mistrust. This is not the first time. The discovery of writing, some said, would liquidate knowledge through memory. The printing press would limit the depth of thought. Even electricity was seen as a silent killer of the peace of the home. All disruption is overwhelming. What makes the difference is our ability to harness the reins of progress and to combine progress with an ethic that is essential in that great leap that will undoubtedly change the world.

I believe that the Maldives can become a developed country by investing in its productive capacity and increasing its productivity, by transforming its economy into one that is fully digitized and driven by artificial intelligence (AI) and, most importantly, by leveraging its natural beauty and marine resources. Boosting productivity will be the key to our economic transformation. We will do that by reforming and strengthening our institutions, increasing our State capacity and leveraging the private sector. We will also identify and implement policies that support investments in key sectors, such as the digital economy.

The Maldives has more than 1,100 islands, spread across 90,000 square kilometres. Enhancing digital connectivity is key to achieving inclusive development, mobilizing economic activity and fostering a more diversified and resilient economy. We believe that the future is intelligence-driven. That is why we are working towards a digital economy that can contribute as much as 15 per cent of our gross domestic product by 2030. That can be achieved through investing in our information and communications technologies infrastructure. We are using and expanding artificial intelligence systems to deliver essential services such as healthcare, education and social welfare. We are also delving into cutting-edge applications of 5G technology, using drones for delivering medical supplies, implementing smart road systems and using AI-enhanced technology for detecting erosion and monitoring the environment.

The transformation can be sustainable only if we transform our education and financial systems. We need to invest in people’s digital literacy from a young age to build a generation that can use artificial intelligence to enhance the delivery of public services, build new products and compete successfully in the global digital economy. We need to bridge the digital divides within our country, including by improving the collection and utilization of data. We need to strengthen our regulatory frameworks, bolster existing institutions, cultivate start-up ecosystems and provide the impetus for the future we envision.

Artificial intelligence, which is presented as a positive element in our daily lives, also facilitates the spread of disinformation campaigns aimed at manipulating public opinion, especially in election periods, thereby destabilizing our democracies. We have a collective responsibility to ensure that new technologies are developed and used with full respect for the dignity, freedom and rights of all people. Clear principles and regulatory frameworks for digital governance must therefore be defined. In that regard, we welcome the Global Digital Compact (resolution 79/1, annex I), adopted at the Summit of the Future.

We live in a turbulent, volatile world that is going through unprecedented and extremely difficult times with tremendous challenges. Those challenges include armed conflicts, tensions in every corner of the globe, crises in multilateral institutions and the international system, a siege on the values of democracy by the twin threats of populism and authoritarianism, risks of cyberwarfare and the inappropriate application of artificial intelligence, the brutal inequity in the distribution of wealth, and climate change, which is endangering our very existence. Those are just some of the immense problems we are facing. I am afraid that I have not come here today to make a speech that will make us feel good, but rather one that will elicit the discomfort and concern that we should be feeling in the face of what is happening. I think that we must be honest and admit that we are failing — all of us — in building a better world. However, if there is a time and a place to debate and propose the crucial decisions that can change the course of humankind, it is the General Assembly. And thanks to the delicate situation we are living in, it is our duty to do so.

As we consolidate our geographical position as a hub of regional integration and logistics development, it is crucial that that vision of growth be backed by a strong investment in education. Paraguay’s success will depend on our ability to prepare future generations for the globalized and competitive world. Along with education, technology is a key tool for development and social inclusion. Our nations face many challenges. However, without a doubt, the question of the ethical application of artificial intelligence and of advances in technology in general stands out here. Moore’s Law postulates an exponential growth in the development of new technologies that require us to create new regulatory schemes to protect people, schemes capable of addressing a challenge that is approaching with a speed that is difficult to grasp. Those new techniques, such as sandboxes and co-regulation, must have as their ultimate goal the responsible use of emerging technologies and the equitable application thereof.

Unfortunately, on behalf of the humanity, we are not doing enough to stop it. If this continues, neither future generations nor history will forgive us. On behalf of the people of Bangladesh and of conscientious citizens across the world, I once again make a strong appeal: the two-state solution must be implemented now through the establishment of an independent state of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital. Only on the basis of the pre-1967 borders, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace, can justice be done. Madam President, In Bangladesh, we believe that we must build a culture of peace, one that rests on the values of tolerance, non-violence, dialogue and cooperation at every level of society. For more than three and a half decades, Bangladesh has stood among the leading contributors of UN peacekeepers. This is living proof of our enduring commitment to global peace and security. Even today, nearly 6,000 Bangladeshi peacekeepers are serving in some of the world's most volatile regions under the UN flag. And 168 of our peacekeepers have made the ultimate sacrifice in line of duty. Research has consistently shown that UN peacekeeping missions are more sustainable and effective than unilateral interventions. We therefore call for clear and achievable mandates and adequate funding for peacekeeping operations. We must also give the highest priority to the safety of peacekeepers and ensure accountability for crimes committed against them. Bangladesh also actively promotes multilingualism, both at home and internationally, because we believe that linguistic and cultural diversity deepens mutual understanding. In the 21st century, There is no place for hatred, intolerance, racism, xenophobia, or Islamophobia in any society. Yet today, disinformation and hate speech have become matters of grave concern. In the aftermath of last year's popular uprising in Bangladesh, certain vested groups deliberately spread false narratives and such disinformation continues even now. The problem has been compounded by the deliberate use of fake news and artificial intelligence-driven deepfakes, which make the situation even more dangerous.

As a sign of our commitment to workers' rights, we have also signed the Charter of the OIC Labour Centre. For these reasons, we strongly support safe, orderly, and regular migration. We call upon all countries that receive migrant workers to ensure empathy and protection for them. While developed nations struggle with aging populations, Bangladesh is blessed. More than 60% of our people are under the age of 35. If migration pathways are opened, it will be mutually beneficial. By harnessing the strength of our youth, we can help meet labor needs in developed countries while creating opportunities for our own people. Madam President, the young generation of Bangladesh has already shown that they are the driving force of social change. We are investing in their skills in information technology, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, and green innovation. Our goal is clear to shape every young person not only as a job seeker but also as a job creator. To this end, in partnership with the UN, we are launching a permanent platform to connect young people at the grassroots with senior policymakers of the government. Across the country, consultations have already begun. Today's youth want to be directly connected to their representatives, from the local to the national level, through online and offline forums, surveys and campaigns. They demand greater opportunities for leadership, skills development, and digital literacy. They call for accountability in this process, with regular progress reports and continuous dialogue. Above all, they insist that the process be inclusive, with equal space for women, minorities, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups. This year is especially significant for youth policy, as we celebrate the 30th anniversary of the World Programme of Action for Youth. It is not only a moment to address the challenges of today's young people, but also to anticipate the crises

they will face tomorrow and to begin shaping the solutions. In this fast-changing technological era, one of our deepest concerns is the widening digital divide facing youth in developing world. Quantum computing, artificial intelligence, large language models, modern communication systems, these must not be biased, and their benefits must be shared fairly with all. If not, we risk creating an entire generation who will see themselves as excluded, marginalized, and treated unjustly. Such a generation will be vulnerable to every harmful temptation. We believe that to shield young people from this risk and to spread the benefits of technology to all, technological innovation alone is not enough. we also need social innovation. Almost half a century ago, we introduced the idea of microcredit. It was then a radical experiment against conventional wisdom. Today, it is a globally recognized tool that has lifted millions out of poverty. In the US, for example, Grameen America has disbursed more than $6.2 billion till date to low income women entrepreneurs with repayment rates close to 100%. Today in Bangladesh and across the world. We are advancing the idea of social business. It is a form of business where profits are entirely reinvested for social good. Social business has shown that the entrepreneurial spirit of every human being can be harnessed for the welfare of society and the solving of social problems. This gives humanity a creative method to address every challenge whether environmental degradation, concentration of wealth, health care, unemployment or poverty. It is a path that can be applied and sustained everywhere. Madam President, In confronting the climate crisis, the goal of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius has already slipped beyond our grasp. The annual pledge of $100 billion in climate finance has not been met. Worse still, the small sums that are disbursed are often shown on paper as many times larger than what they really are. This is unacceptable. For the sake of our children's future, we must act now. The Loss and Damage Fund must be made fully operational.

Today in the world, there is greater inequality in the distribution of wealth than there was 80 years ago. the poverty figures, inequality and injustice, rather than being curbed, is on the increase. The risk that any remaining peace should disappear and the third world war would overtake the entire planet is very close if we don't react in time. The danger here is that the unstoppable force of capitalism with the misuse of artificial intelligence would increase the climate change, would liquidate the planet and would convert the immense majority of the population into unnecessary beings is also something that we can't completely rule out. We're not in a good place. The UN was established on the basis of the foundations of the skeletons of the Holocaust and the not only physical but also moral ruins left by the fascist racism and also increasing neocolonialism with the use of two atomic bombs. One of the goals that gave rise to the United Nations was to not repeat the barbarity of war. Today we hear the echoes of the drums of war on all continents. We see the practice of genocide on the sole decision of two countries. We deny the right to be free and sovereign to a people, sovereign sophisticated weapons are used against a sovereign country and increasing militarization is being promoted within a region with double standards in combating the war on drugs and at the same time we maintain a criminal blockade against its people and the state for the sole crime of having claimed its own independence more than six decades ago. Wars not the same as we had 80 years ago. Wars now are multidimensional. They use economic, financial, media, information, cyber warfare. without even taking into account military warfare, which now encompasses biological warfare, war from space, and other technologies that continue to be developed with impunity on the basis of technology of war. It would be nothing new to have climate wars that would have an impact on sovereignty and food security.

Madam President, Excellencies, Costa Rica congratulates you on your election to preside over the 80th session of the General Assembly. You can count on the firm and unwavering support of my country in contributing to the success of your tenure. Eight decades ago, we embarked on the journey to San Francisco to save humanity from the abyss of war. Together, throughout this journey, we codified human rights and built an international system based on the rule of law. We established the foundations of our collective security system and generated global processes for environmental protection and the development of nations. We achieved the decolonization of more than 80 territories and mediated in hundreds of conflicts. Today, however, the mission faces three significant global challenges: nuclear weapons, the triple planetary crisis, and the governance of artificial intelligence. In the same year that we founded this organization, humanity crossed a threshold when Hiroshima and Nagasaki were reduced to ruins in an instant by atomic bombs. Today, the risk of nuclear conflict is the highest it has been in decades. Trust is eroding. Geopolitical tensions are widening. The shadow of the use of nuclear weapons looms once again. Nuclear weapons are once again being considered by their possessors as central to national security strategies and are wielded as tools of coercion. Any nuclear detonation, whether intentional or accidental, would have irreversible humanitarian environmental consequences. There is no possible humanitarian response. There is no margin for error. 55 years after the entry into force of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and looking ahead to its 2026 review conference, nuclear weapons states will have a new opportunity to reaffirm their adherence to the treaty and to the obligations and commitments they have undertaken as States Parties, particularly Article VI. We also urge you to recognize that the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons strengthens and complements the NPT, and it represents a decisive step toward fulfilling the very first resolution adopted by this Assembly and an essential element of the nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation regime.

That is why Costa Rica is driving the process of concluding a binding treaty on plastic pollution that covers its entire life cycle, advancing scientific research, and calling for a precautionary pause on deep sea mining, as well as urging the full implementation of the BBNJ treaty with conservation as its top priority. Time is running out to respond to these threats that do not recognize any borders. Time is also running out to bridge the digital divide and confront a technological revolution driven by artificial intelligence that is advancing at high speed. Artificial intelligence can strengthen our national economies and our collective efforts to achieve development. It can optimize resources. accelerate medical research, and democratize access to knowledge. But it can also divide us between those who have access and those who do not. Artificial intelligence also poses risks to international peace and security. It can become a vector of mass disinformation and enable cyber attacks that paralyze critical infrastructure. Artificial intelligence also challenges our ability to maintain meaningful human control over life or death decisions as military automation advances without adequate regulatory frameworks. Establishing such frameworks is urgent and time is running out. One application of AI that deserves special attention is autonomous weapons systems. Costa Rica urges the conclusion before 2026 of a legally binding instrument that establishes prohibitions and regulations for autonomous weapons systems capable of identifying, selecting, and attacking targets without meaningful human control. No algorithm should ever make life or death decisions. Madam President, Excellencies, Costa Rica has demonstrated for decades that our impact in this organization is not determined by our size. Small states lead through action. We build bridges and forge consensuses that once seemed distant. That is how we move forward. That is how we prove that together we're stronger and that this is our common home. Just this year, Costa Rica, in the face of the most devastating humanitarian crisis since the founding of the United Nations, together with 150 states, launched a call to action while chairing the Humanitarian Affairs segment of the Economic and Social Council.

Faced with the grave humanitarian consequences of the use of explosive weapons in populated areas, Costa Rica will host the Second International Conference on the Political Declaration on Strengthening the Protection of Civilians to be held in San Jose from 18th to 20th of November. In light of the risks and opportunities posed by artificial intelligence, Costa Rica, together with Spain, has led the process that established the independent international scientific panel and the global dialogue on AI governance to be launched tomorrow. Its adoption by consensus is a milestone in itself. Faced with the urgency of protecting the environment and the ocean, Costa Rica co-organized with France UNOC 3, where we reached significant political and financial commitments for ocean governance and health. In confronting the persistent inequalities that limit the dignity and rights of women and girls, together with Cabo Verde, Costa Rica achieved the adoption by consensus of the political declaration marking the 30th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women, and Costa Rica, with great responsibility and commitment, assumed the presidency of the 70th session of the Commission on the Status of Women. Madam President, Excellencies, the person who will hold the office of Secretary-General as of January 2027 must have the leadership and vision required to face the three great global challenges, the vision that comes from experience, and the courage that only years of service at the highest level can provide. What is required is authority that is born of integrity. It must be a person who embraces with wisdom and conviction the three pillars of this organization. Someone who forges consensus and inspires hope, even in the most difficult. circumstances, someone with the determination to renew and strengthen this organization. We are confident that we will find that person and we are confident also that we will find that person in our region because it is a turn of Latin America and the Caribbean. The world has changed and our organization must change with it.

We're suffering the consequences of powerful cultural domination in an era when digital technology increasingly impacts our lives across the board. A few transnationals, almost all of them from the US, impose their operating systems and control the content that is seen, read and heard, manipulating human behaviour. We are suffering from the dictatorship of the algorithm. What we need to do is establish at the UN as soon as possible common norms in order to unlock the transformative potential of new technologies, especially artificial intelligence, for the benefit of all. whilst at the same time mitigating the risks. Beyond the challenges that Cuba faces as a small island developing state, our country suffers from the devastating and accumulated impact of the policy of hostility and economic suffocation that has been imposed by the United States for more than six decades. The blockade against Cuba persists and is being tightened to the extreme.
